title: Check yourself: Compliance, fairness, transparency and the register

questions.stem: Scenario: Mira is asked to honour a deletion request from a customer whose requests appear in the audit entries of a claims assistant. Those entries hold tokens, and one table maps each token to a person. What does the design do?

options.text: Delete the entries of that customer from the log
options.says: Ruled out because "Deleting every audit entry would destroy the proof".

options.text: Remove the vault rows that tie them to anything in the log
options.says: Removing the vault rows leaves the entries and unlinks them from the person.

options.text: Replace the tokens in that customer's entries with new tokens
options.says: Ruled out because "keeping both leaves the person identifiable", and new tokens in the entries leave the vault map in place.

options.text: Encrypt that customer's entries with a key that is then kept
options.says: Ruled out because the design removes "the map: the vault entries for that person go", and encryption keeps a key that can link them again.

questions.stem: Scenario: Tomas must set how long a support assistant keeps its audit records. Tomas's design has a shortest period, a longest period and a number of days between them. A court order then opens a case that covers a set of those records. What happens to those records?

options.text: They are deleted at once because the court may inspect any copy
options.says: Ruled out because the hold keeps records, as "the records in scope are kept past it".

options.text: They follow the same schedule and the case uses what is left
options.says: Ruled out because "A legal hold is the one thing that outranks the ceiling", so the ordinary schedule does not apply.

options.text: They are moved to a table with no limit on their retention
options.says: Ruled out because "they are released when the hold ends", and an unlimited table keeps them after the case.

options.text: They are held past the ceiling until the matter is settled
options.says: A legal hold is the one thing that outranks the ceiling, and the records are released when it ends.

origin.section: Retention: a floor, a ceiling and a legal hold
